findings.title: Cache deletion does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status in the UI
findings.body: The `deleteCache` mutation's `onSuccess` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop; unlike the `disconnectMutation` right below it, it never calls `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`. The `cacheUpdatedAt` shown in the dropdown comes from that query, so after a successful deletion the menu keeps displaying "Cache Status / Last updated ..." and the "Delete cached data" item until some other action refetches. In usages where `onChanged` is not passed (or does not invalidate this query) the UI is simply wrong after the action. Invalidate `connectedCalendars` in `onSettled` as the disconnect path does.

findings.title: Extra updateMany on every Google webhook writes to SelectedCalendar for no consumer
findings.body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` is invoked by the Google Calendar webhook handler on every push notification. The new `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` issues an additional UPDATE across all SelectedCalendar rows for the credential on each notification purely to bump `@updatedAt`. The PR description itself states this value is not used by the frontend (the UI reads `CalendarCache.updatedAt`), so this is a dead write on a hot path. It also repurposes `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` (configuration change time) to mean "cache refreshed", which will confuse anyone relying on that column's original semantics. Remove it or scope it to an actual consumer.

findings.title: No tests for the new mutation, repository method, or handler enrichment
findings.body: The PR adds a new authenticated mutation (`deleteCacheHandler` with an ownership check), a new repository query (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` using `groupBy`/`_max`), and changes the shape of `connectedCalendarsHandler`'s output (`cacheUpdatedAt`), but adds no unit or integration tests for any of them. The description notes local testing was not possible. At minimum the handler should have tests for: deleting cache for an owned credential, rejecting a credential owned by another user, and the connectedCalendars enrichment mapping (including credentials with no cache rows and negative/delegation credential ids).

findings.title: Cache status ignores expiresAt, so expired cache rows are reported as live cache
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `CalendarCache` rows by `credentialId` and takes `MAX(updatedAt)` without filtering on `expiresAt >= now()`. Every read path (`getCachedAvailability`) treats rows past `expiresAt` as non-existent, so a credential whose only cache rows have expired will still show "Cache Status: Last updated ..." in the UI even though no cache is actually being served. Add `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to the `where` clause so the status reflects what the cache layer will actually use.

findings.title: Timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded en-US locale and browser timezone
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the user's locale even though the component already calls `useLocale()`, and formats in the browser's timezone rather than the user's profile timezone/time format used elsewhere in the app. Non-English users will see an English-formatted date inside an otherwise translated menu, and users whose profile timezone differs from the browser will see a misleading time. Use the locale from `useLocale()` (or the existing dayjs/timeFormat helpers) instead.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId that nothing in the PR reads
findings.body: `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` were changed from `Pick<SelectedCalendar, "externalId" | "integration" | "eventTypeId">` to also require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`, and `findUnlockedUserForSession` was widened to select them. No code in this PR consumes these fields (the UI uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt`), so this tightens the public type contract of `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` (also re-exported via `@calcom/platform-libraries` to API v2) and enlarges the session user payload for no benefit. Any caller that builds a `UserWithCalendars` from a narrower select will now fail to type-check. Revert unless a consumer is added.

findings.title: Unexplained removal of `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` loses compile-time validation
findings.body: `findMany` previously asserted `{ where, select, orderBy } satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs`, which guaranteed the hand-written `FindManyArgs` type stays compatible with Prisma's generated types. The PR removes this with no explanation and it is unrelated to the feature. Without it, drift between `FindManyArgs` and the Prisma schema will only surface as a runtime Prisma validation error instead of a type error.

findings.title: Handler throws a plain Error (500) and fetches the full credential row including secrets
findings.body: When the credential is not found or not owned by the user, the handler throws `new Error(...)`, which tRPC surfaces as `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` rather than `NOT_FOUND`/`FORBIDDEN`, so clients and logs cannot distinguish an authorization failure from a server fault. Additionally `prisma.credential.findFirst` has no `select`, so it loads the entire row including the encrypted OAuth `key` just to check existence. Use `TRPCError` with an appropriate code and `select: { id: true }`.

findings.title: ENV_FILE is resolved relative to the caller's CWD, not the script location
findings.body: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` assumes the script is executed from inside `scripts/`. Running it the natural way from the repo root (`./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`) makes it read/modify `<parent-of-repo>/.env`, and because the script `touch`es the file when missing it will silently create a `.env` outside the repository and never update the real one. Resolve the path from `$(dirname "$0")/../.env` instead.

findings.title: `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS-only and fails on GNU sed
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E "s|...|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses the BSD form of in-place editing. With GNU sed (Linux, most CI/dev containers) the empty string is parsed as the sed script and the substitution expression is treated as a filename, producing "can't read s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=...: No such file" and leaving `.env` unchanged. Use a portable approach (e.g. write to a temp file and `mv`, or detect the platform).

findings.title: Failure paths exit with status 0
findings.body: `cleanup` always runs `exit 0`, and it is also used as the exit path for error conditions (rate limit hit, failed to extract tunnel URL). Callers or wrappers cannot detect that the script failed, and the `.env` may not have been updated even though the exit code says success. Error paths should exit non-zero.

findings.title: dev:cron switched to `npx tsx` which is not a declared dependency
findings.body: `dev:cron` was changed from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` is not listed in `dependencies`/`devDependencies` (while `ts-node` remains). `npx` will fetch an arbitrary latest `tsx` from the registry at run time, making the script non-reproducible and requiring network access. This change is also unrelated to the PR. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency and call it directly, or keep `ts-node`.

findings.title: Migration header warning contradicts the actual statement
findings.body: The generated warning says the column was added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the statement below explicitly adds `DEFAULT NOW()` (and the schema has `@default(now())`). The stale warning will mislead anyone auditing migrations into thinking this migration is unsafe on populated tables. Remove or correct the comment.
